questions.prompt: An allowed-locations policy is assigned to management group Production. A subscription beneath it has no exclusion or exemption. Where is the policy relevant?

options.text: Applicable resources in the descendant subscription.
options.explanation: Governance assignments inherit down the hierarchy.

options.text: Only the management group display-name property.
options.explanation: The purpose is governing descendant resources.
Sibling branches are not the assignment's descendants.

options.text: Every subscription in every Entra tenant.
options.explanation: Management-group scope does not span unrelated tenants.

questions.prompt: Can one Azure subscription simultaneously be a direct child of two management groups?

options.text: No; it has one parent in the hierarchy.
options.explanation: Use a hierarchy and assignments consistent with that single-parent model.

options.text: Yes, one parent for Policy and another for RBAC.
options.explanation: Those controls use the same management hierarchy.

options.text: Yes, if it has two billing contacts.
options.explanation: Billing contacts do not create multiple hierarchy parents.

options.text: Yes, one parent for every Azure region it uses.
options.explanation: Resource regions do not determine management-group parent count.

questions.prompt: A subscription moves from Sandbox to Production management group in the same tenant. Which effect should be reviewed?

options.text: Changes to inherited Policy and RBAC assignments.
options.explanation: The new ancestor chain can change effective governance.

options.text: Automatic regional relocation of its VMs.
options.explanation: The hierarchy move is not a data-center move.

options.text: Automatic creation of a new Entra directory.
options.explanation: The scenario remains within the existing tenant.

options.text: Replacement of every resource's subscription ID.
options.explanation: A management-group move does not create a new subscription.
